verification_evidence.no_rake_leak_into_wall_lanes: Even with a measured rake (36.06 LF) on screen: photo-takeoff-trim-lf-starter='—' (named refusal: 'no wall BASE is marked on this photo…'), photo-takeoff-trim-lf-outside_corner='—' (named refusal: 'no corner is marked on this photo, and no wall here carries a confirmed height…'), photo-takeoff-trim-lf-inside_corner='—' (same named corner refusal), photo-takeoff-trim-lf-soffit='—', photo-takeoff-trim-lf-fascia='—' (fascia refusal explicitly states 'The GABLE RAKE is measured separately, from the rake lines already drawn'). Rake did NOT leak into any wall lane.
verification_evidence.no_zero_defect: Full-panel text scan: every real figure is 18 LF, 18.0 LF, 36.06 LF, 3.0 ft, 6.0 ft, 30.0 ft, 10.0 ft. No bare '0' or '0 LF' appears in any row as a measurement. (The literal string 'never a 0' inside the flat-gable refusal sentence is the intended print, not a defect.)

critical_code_review_comments: TrimPanel.jsx remains a pure printer — every LF and every refusal comes from qty.trim_rows on the server. lf() prints '—' whenever the figure is null, so the em-dash-not-zero contract is upheld structurally.

Backend _gable_rake correctly zones the row (GABLE ZONE tag rendered) and per-gable lines carry span/rise/LF from the rake lines actually drawn — 30 ft span + 10 ft rise resolves to hypotenuse √(15²+10²)=18.028 per side × 2 = 36.056 ≈ 36.06 LF, math checks out.
Flat gable (rise=0) is refused with 'NO RISE' language and explicit 'never a 0' — no factor is invented and no fallback to 0.
